title: How I work
lede: Van Gogh painted the view from a barred window and turned it into the most famous sky in the world. The constraint was not the obstacle. It was the subject.

movements.heading: Ask what they came for
movements.body: Nobody opens an app to admire it. They open it to find out whether it will rain, or where the mechanic has got to, or who plays next. I try to name that sentence before I open Figma, because every layout decision after it is downstream of getting it right.

movements.heading: The small stuff is the job
movements.body: Spacing, weight, the half-second a transition takes. On their own these look like fussing. Together they are the entire difference between an interface someone trusts and one they merely tolerate.

movements.heading: Design the waiting
movements.body: The happy path is the easy part. Most of my time goes on the states around it — loading, empty, failed, halfway there — because that is where people actually are when something matters to them.

movements.heading: Publish before it is safe
movements.body: Everything in the last room went up while I could still see what was wrong with it. Working where it can be seen is slower and more uncomfortable, and it is the only reason any of it improved.
